title: SGH Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: SGH Group employee
tiers.description: All Non-Executive Directors, Officers and employees of SGH and SGH's subsidiaries. Bound by the insider trading restriction and by the blackout periods, but not by the window periods or the general prior-clearance requirement, which apply only to Executives and designated employees.

tiers.name: Designated employees
tiers.description: Any Non-Executive Director or Officer; any direct report to the SGH Managing Director & CEO; any member of the Executive Leadership Team of an SGH Group subsidiary and those within their department who assist them; any employee of the SGH Corporate Office; and any other employee prescribed by the Company Secretary from time to time. May deal only in the window periods, or outside them with prior written clearance.

tiers.name: Executives
tiers.description: Executives, named alongside designated employees as the group with access to confidential and price-sensitive information. Subject to the window and clearance regime and to the absolute blackout-period ban on dealing in financial products issued or created over or in respect of SGH securities.

tiers.name: Chairman of the Board
tiers.description: The Chairman in his or her own dealing capacity; clearance from the Lead Independent Director or Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Managing Director & CEO
tiers.description: The Managing Director & CEO in his or her own dealing capacity; clearance from the Chairman of the Board, the Lead Independent Director or the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Directors (other than the Chairman of the Board)
tiers.description: Directors other than the Chairman; clearance from the Chairman of the Board.

tiers.name: Company Secretary
tiers.description: The SGH Company Secretary in his or her own dealing capacity; clearance from the Managing Director & CEO. The Company Secretary is also the approver for all other designated employees and the recipient of dealing notifications.

tiers.name: Direct Reports to the Managing Director & CEO
tiers.description: Direct reports to the SGH Managing Director & CEO; clearance from the Managing Director & CEO. Together with SGH Corporate Office employees they carry the additional pre-notification and post-trade notification obligations in section 6.

tiers.name: All other designated employees
tiers.description: Designated employees other than the Chairman, MD & CEO, other Directors, the Company Secretary and MD & CEO direct reports; clearance from the SGH Company Secretary. Non-designated employees who need blackout-period approval also go to the SGH Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Spouses, partners, family members, family trusts, superannuation funds and any other connected person of an SGH Group employee. Associates of designated employees must comply with the policy as if they were a designated employee, and a breach by an associate is a breach by the employee.

definitions.hedging_definition: Other financial products that operate to limit the economic risk of holding SGH shares

windows.end_anchor: 30 working days after the release of SGH's Annual Results announcement to the ASX

windows.end_anchor: 30 working days after the close of SGH's Annual General Meeting

windows.start_anchor: the last day of the financial year
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after the release of SGH's Annual Results announcement to the ASX

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board or its delegate may determine 'any other period' to be a blackout period for the purposes of the policy. The policy does not state whether such a determination is confidential or how it is communicated.

rules.detail: Options and other financial products issued over SGH shares by third parties, associated products, and products that limit the economic risk of holding SGH shares are all defined as SGH securities. There is no venue restriction and no outright ban, so an OTC put bought from a bank and a call written to it are dealings that a designated employee may do inside a window period, or outside a window with prior written clearance from the relevant approver.
rules.evidence: Options or other financial products issued over these classes of SGH shares by third parties, or associated products; Other financial products that operate to limit the economic risk of holding SGH shares.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options over SGH shares are treated identically; the definition of SGH securities draws no distinction between listed and OTC products.
rules.evidence: Options or other financial products issued over these classes of SGH shares by third parties, or associated products

rules.detail: During blackout periods the ban on dealing in financial products issued or created over or in respect of SGH securities is absolute for Executives and designated staff, and unlike the ordinary blackout ban it carries no exceptional circumstances relief. Outside blackout periods the ordinary window and clearance regime applies.
rules.evidence: In addition, during the blackout periods, no Executives or designated staff may deal in financial products issued or created over or in respect of SGH securities. No exceptional circumstances exemption applies to this prohibition.

rules.detail: Employees who are neither Executives nor designated employees are not subject to the window periods or the prior clearance requirement. They are bound only by the insider trading restriction and by the general blackout-period ban, from which they may seek an exceptional-circumstances waiver from the SGH Company Secretary.
rules.evidence: In addition, designated employees are permitted to deal in SGH securities only as follows

rules.detail: Remarkably, the policy contains no prohibition on hedging. Products that operate to limit the economic risk of holding SGH shares are simply brought within the definition of SGH securities, so hedging is regulated like any other dealing: inside a window period, or outside it with prior written clearance from the relevant approver, and never during a blackout period.
rules.evidence: Other financial products that operate to limit the economic risk of holding SGH shares.

rules.detail: There is no ban on hedging unvested or unexercised employee share plan entitlements, which is unusual for an ASX policy. Participation in an SGH Employee Share Plan itself needs no approval or notification, but dealing in shares attained from employee share plans remains subject to the policy, so a hedge referencing plan securities is a dealing in SGH securities requiring a window or clearance.
rules.evidence: Dealing in shares attained from employee share plans is still subject to this policy.

rules.detail: Restricted shares are recognised (lifting restrictions on restricted shares needs no approval) but no separate hedging or encumbrance restriction attaches to them; the ordinary window and clearance regime governs.
rules.evidence: A SGH Group employee is not required to seek approval or provide notification in connection with participation in any SGH Employee Share Plan, which includes: ... Lifting restrictions on restricted shares.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a collar-plus-loan, prepaid forward or similar is both a financial product limiting the economic risk of holding SGH shares and, where secured, a dealing pursuant to a lending arrangement. Both limbs point to the same answer: written clearance from the relevant approver, which may be granted subject to conditions.
rules.evidence: Other financial products that operate to limit the economic risk of holding SGH shares.

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the policy. A short sale would still be a 'sell' and therefore a dealing subject to the window, clearance and blackout regime, but there is no separate prohibition on it.
Securities lending and borrowing are not mentioned and are outside the definition of Deal, which covers only buying and selling and procuring others to buy or sell.

CFDs are not named but a contract for difference over SGH shares is a financial product issued over SGH shares by a third party, or an associated product, and so is an SGH security. Dealing in it therefore requires a window period or prior written clearance, and is absolutely barred for Executives and designated staff in a blackout period.
rules.evidence: Options or other financial products issued over these classes of SGH shares by third parties, or associated products

rules.detail: Margin lending is expressly permitted, not banned. Entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of SGH securities, transferring SGH securities into an existing margin loan account, and selling SGH securities held in a margin loan account are each dealings requiring written clearance from the relevant approver, who may impose conditions. The employee must not participate in the decision on their own application.
rules.evidence: Any dealing in SGH securities by a SGH Group employee pursuant to a margin lending arrangement must comply with this policy. Such dealings may include entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of SGH securities, transferring SGH securities into an existing margin loan account and selling SGH securities held in a margin loan account.

rules.detail: Granting security over SGH securities is not itself within the definition of Deal, but section 5 treats entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of SGH securities and transferring securities into a margin loan account as dealings requiring written clearance. An encumbrance unconnected with a lending arrangement is not addressed.
rules.evidence: Such dealings may include entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of SGH securities, transferring SGH securities into an existing margin loan account

rules.detail: Only margin lending arrangements are named. A bank loan secured on SGH shares is not expressly covered, but section 5 is drafted broadly around 'any dealing in SGH securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement' and the prudent reading, consistent with the section 8 carve-out for secured lender enforcement, is that a share-secured facility must be cleared in the same way. There is no prohibition on secured financing anywhere in the policy.
rules.evidence: Any dealing in SGH securities by a SGH Group employee pursuant to a margin lending arrangement must comply with this policy.

rules.detail: The policy contains no short-term trading, speculative trading or minimum holding period restriction of any kind. The only timing constraints are the window periods, the blackout periods and the two-business-day validity of a clearance.

clearance.approver: Lead Independent Director / Chair of the ARC
clearance.evidence: Chairman of the Board | Lead Independent Director/Chair of the ARC ... Clearance may be given in any written form and is effective for two business days after it has been given.

clearance.approver: Chairman of the Board / Lead Independent Director / Chair of the ARC
clearance.evidence: Managing Director & CEO | Chairman of the Board/Lead Independent Director/Chair of the ARC

clearance.tier: Directors (other than the Chairman of the Board)
clearance.evidence: Directors (other than the Chairman of the Board) | Chairman of the Board

clearance.tier: Direct Reports to the Managing Director & CEO
clearance.post_trade_to: SGH Company Secretary (who must notify the SGH Managing Director & CEO)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two business days of the trade being entered into, i.e. before the trade has settled; plus notice of intention not less than two trading days before any proposed dealing in a trading window
clearance.evidence: All direct reports to the SGH Managing Director & CEO and employees in the SGH Corporate Office must notify the SGH Company Secretary of their intention to deal in securities during a trading window, not less than two (2) trading days prior to any proposed dealing. They must also notify the SGH Company Secretary of any dealings within two business days of the trade being entered into i.e. before the trade has settled.

clearance.post_trade_to: SGH Company Secretary (SGH Corporate Office employees only)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two business days of the trade being entered into (SGH Corporate Office employees only)
clearance.evidence: All other designated employees | SGH Company Secretary

clearance.approver: SGH Company Secretary (only required for dealing during a blackout period)
clearance.evidence: For any employee who is not classified as a designated employee, they will need to obtain approval from the SGH Company Secretary.

exceptions.approver: the relevant approver in the section 3 table; SGH Company Secretary for non-designated employees
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances are circumstances where the approver is satisfied that the proposed dealing is the most reasonable course of action available. Exceptional circumstances may include: Extreme financial hardship

exceptions.approver: the relevant approver in the section 3 table

exceptions.evidence: Any other circumstance determined by the Board or its delegate to be exceptional.

A disposal of SGH securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a margin lending arrangement, where this policy has been complied with in relation to the margin lending arrangement.

Dealings where there is no effective change in the beneficial owner (such as a transfer from the SGH Group employee to a family trust or to a self-managed superannuation fund of which the SGH Group employee is a beneficiary)
Passive trades such as the acquisition of SGH securities through a dividend reinvestment plan, a share purchase plan available to all retail shareholders, a rights issue
or the sale of SGH securities arising as a result of acceptance of a takeover offer

A SGH Group employee is not required to seek approval or provide notification in connection with participation in any SGH Employee Share Plan, which includes: Applying for an allocation of securities pursuant to an employee share offer; Exercising vested rights or options; and Lifting restrictions on restricted shares.

financing_disclosure: Direct Reports to the Managing Director & CEO and SGH Corporate Office employees: trigger is any dealing, including a dealing in connection with a margin lending arrangement; to the SGH Company Secretary (who notifies the MD & CEO); notice of intention not less than two trading days before dealing in a window, and notice of the dealing within two business days of the trade being entered into, before settlement.

exemption_authority: The approver named in the section 3 table (and the SGH Company Secretary for non-designated employees) may grant a written waiver to deal during a blackout period in exceptional circumstances, being where the approver is satisfied the proposed dealing is the most reasonable course of action available. The Board or its delegate may determine any other circumstance to be exceptional and may determine additional blackout periods. The one exemption expressly withheld is the blackout-period ban on Executives and designated staff dealing in financial products issued or created over or in respect of SGH securities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no clause prohibiting hedging. Instead, 'Other financial products that operate to limit the economic risk of holding SGH shares' are simply included in the definition of SGH securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the key enabling feature: a collar is regulated as an ordinary dealing needing a window or clearance, rather than banned, and there is no ban on hedging unvested or restricted plan securities either.

bespoke_clauses.topic: absolute blackout ban on derivative products
bespoke_clauses.clause: In addition, during the blackout periods, no Executives or designated staff may deal in financial products issued or created over or in respect of SGH securities. No exceptional circumstances exemption applies to this prohibition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar entry, roll, unwind or any adjustment involving the option legs is absolutely impossible in a blackout period, with no hardship or court-order relief, so the bank must build hard date constraints into the trade.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any designated employee must obtain clearance in writing from the relevant approver detailed in the table in Section 3 for any proposed dealing in SGH securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement. ... Clearance may be granted subject to any conditions the approver determines appropriate.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is permitted with clearance rather than prohibited, and the approver's power to impose conditions gives the company a way to protect itself rather than refuse outright.

bespoke_clauses.clause: this policy does not apply to: ... A disposal of SGH securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a margin lending arrangement, where this policy has been complied with in relation to the margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Lender enforcement over the collared shares, including in a blackout period, is outside the policy, but only if the underlying facility was itself properly cleared, so the bank should make clearance a condition precedent and retain evidence of it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Clearance may be given in any written form and is effective for two business days after it has been given.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar and the loan must be documented in advance and executed within two business days of clearance, so pricing and legal work must be complete before the approval is sought.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In the period between 24 hours and 30 working days after the release of SGH's Half Yearly Results announcement ... Annual Results announcements ... and the close of the SGHs Annual General Meeting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Three 30-working-day windows a year give ample scope to strike or unwind a collar without needing discretionary clearance at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A designated employee must not be involved in a decision regarding their own application for clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For a Chairman or CEO collar the approval must come from the Lead Independent Director or ARC Chair, so the bank should verify who signed the clearance.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no short-term or speculative trading rule
bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy imposes no minimum holding period and no restriction on short-term or speculative dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar tenor is unconstrained by the policy, so short-dated or rolling structures are not objectionable on their face.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Deal includes buying and selling, as well as procuring others to buy or sell.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Granting security is not literally a Deal, so section 5 rather than the general definition is what brings the loan and any share transfer into the clearance net; a pledge unconnected to a lending arrangement sits in a gap.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associates of designated employees must comply with the policy as if they were a designated employee ... A breach of this policy, including a breach by an associate, will be regarded as serious misconduct.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar through a family trust or superannuation fund attracts the identical window, clearance and blackout constraints and the employee bears the consequences.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All designated employees and their associates must obtain approval prior to trading in the securities of listed entities in which SGH has a Substantial Interest (including controlled and associated entities) [Appendix 1: Beach Energy (BPT), Boral (BLD), Seven West Media (SWM)].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar over Beach Energy, Boral or Seven West Media shares held by an SGH designated employee also requires prior approval under this policy.

summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, and this is one of the more permissive ASX policies for the purpose. There is no hedging prohibition at all: products that limit the economic risk of holding SGH shares are simply defined as SGH securities, so the put and call legs are dealings that a designated employee may execute inside one of the three 30-working-day window periods following the half year results, annual results and AGM, or outside a window with prior written clearance from the approver named in the section 3 table. Margin lending is likewise expressly permitted with written clearance, which may be granted subject to conditions, and a disposal by a secured lender exercising its rights is carved out of the policy entirely provided the facility itself was cleared, which protects the bank on enforcement. The two hard constraints are that no Executive or designated staff member may deal in any financial product issued or created over or in respect of SGH securities during a blackout period, with no exceptional circumstances relief, and that clearance lapses after two business days, so the trade must be fully documented before approval is sought. There is no ban on hedging unvested or restricted plan securities and no short-term trading or minimum holding rule, so vesting state and tenor are not obstacles.
